task_name: NIGHTFORM - Low Beam music release package
client_brief:
Low Beam is the next release. What I need is short form: a teaser, an upright cutdown and the cover, and all three should feel like one night.

The picture in the pack is silent and short, so this is cut picture over music, nothing else. The cleared Low Beam instrumental excerpt is in the pack as nightform_bed.wav. Cut to that excerpt, let the picture move with it, and finish on a phrase rather than stopping mid note. There is no voice on this release and there should not be one on the films. The lines from the caption sheet carry the words, set on screen: any line you use appears in full and word for word, and no line is invented.

The commission

Low Beam release teaser: one named export, wide, twelve to fifteen seconds, music. The picture responds to the excerpt, the release details are accurate (the artist name and the release line word for word as the caption sheet gives them, in the type system's capitals where it sets them) and the last frame holds on them. At least three different shots, no looping one clip to fill the length.

Low Beam vertical cutdown: one named export, upright, eight to ten seconds, music, cut only from shots that also appear in the teaser, at least three different ones. Same night, same road, with the release line readable at arm's length on a dark moving frame.

Music release cover: one named export, square still. The artist name as the caption sheet's ARTIST NAME line has it and the track name spelled exactly as the formats file's Title Line has it, set in the type system's capitals, wordmark from the supplied file, nothing ornamented or distressed.

It is one drive, north of the city, around eleven at night. Any new footage follows that direction: the same wet road, the same sodium light, no daylight, no second location and no people introduced into it.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Video delivery means a playable MP4, not a storyboard, a still montage PDF or an editing log. Audio expectations are stated on each film, and no film in this pack carries speech.

Live action edits require adequate distinct footage. Looping a short clip is not a substitute for the missing coverage.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Self released independent electronic music. Streaming first, with physical vinyl and cassette editions through independent record shops.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: A solo project running since 2020 in Portland, Oregon. One artist who writes, produces and releases everything without a label.
brand_identity.about: NIGHTFORM is a self released electronic project built on mood: late, atmospheric, cinematic tracks that sound like driving at night. The next single, Low Beam, is bought on feeling and on the sense that one person made the whole thing, so every visual has to carry the same nocturnal weight as the music.
brand_identity.audience: Streaming listeners roughly nineteen to thirty four who follow the mood. Physical buyers pay twelve to twenty eight dollars for vinyl and cassette through independent shops.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Independent, no label, priced as a self released record. The look has to be dark, grainy and slightly rough, never bright, clean and commercial, which would read as a car advert or a stock reel. Total blackness is the other failure: the road still has to be legible on a phone in daylight.

brand_identity.typography: NIGHTFORM runs Folio for display and Söhne for text. Step 01, Display / H1, is Folio Medium capitals at 96 px on 104 px leading, letterspaced 0.24 em, for example LOW BEAM, optically fitted to the exact width of the recovered wordmark above it and set at 30 pt on 33 pt on the sleeve. Step 02, Subheading / H2, is the same Folio Medium capitals at 72 px on 80 px leading, still 0.24 em and still width fitted, for the teaser, for example OUT FRIDAY. Step 03, Body, is Söhne Buch 400 at 30 px on 42 px leading, tracking 0, max 65 characters, carrying credits and formats, 8.5 pt on 12 pt in print. Step 04, Fine print, is Söhne Buch 400 at 22 px on 30 px leading, tracking +0.04 em, numerals tabular lining, 7 pt on 10 pt in print. A title never breaks onto two lines.
brand_identity.voice: Spare and evocative, closer to a liner note than a sales line. Example line the brand would write: "Low Beam. Recorded from the passenger seat, north of the city, around eleven at night."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark survives only as a flat exported picture: separated white capitals on a solid black square, from a source file no one still has. It has to be recovered as usable artwork. The previous release's sleeve card exists only as the printer's press PDF, and the whole visual identity for this single comes out of one forty five second night take.
brand_identity.values: One person, one mood, made without a label. The artist changes the words up to the drop date and cannot re commission, so anything text bearing has to stay editable.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: The track title is set in Folio Medium capitals letterspaced 0.24 em and optically fitted to the exact width of the recovered wordmark above it, so every release reads as two white lines of identical measure, one tight and one airy.

rules: Never break a title onto two lines.
The recovered wordmark stays untouched artwork and is never retyped.
The title is always optically fitted to the exact width of the wordmark above it, at 0.24 em letterspacing.
Never bright, clean and commercial; never so black the road stops reading on a phone in daylight.
Anything text bearing stays editable up to the drop date.

palette_rules.distribution: On the films and the cover, grounds are night footage or a solid Asphalt Black, Wet Slate or Low Beam Grey panel, and every line of type is Tunnel White, while the wordmark keeps the white of nightform_wordmark.png. A Tunnel White ground belongs only to printed board, where type is Asphalt Black with a thin Sodium Amber rule beneath the wordmark, as on nightform_card_2024.pdf. Sodium Amber is a thin rule or divider only, never a ground, a panel or type; Sodium Amber and Low Beam Grey rules and dividers together take no more than 5% of the designed, non-footage area.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity; no tint, transparency, gradient, shadow or blend mode; no scrim, gradient, vignette or overlay of any colour, black and white included, laid over footage or a photograph.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the five palette hexes for type, panels, rules or icons (the recovered wordmark keeps its own artwork); no texture or distress on any type, since nothing is ornamented or distressed; no bright, clean, commercial treatment of type or ground.
palette_rules.photography: Footage keeps its own colour and is not recoloured toward the palette hexes: sodium lamps stay amber and the road stays its own colour. It is never lifted into a bright, clean commercial look; a darker, grainier grade toward the brand's night look is allowed as long as the road still reads on a phone in daylight. The near-black low-key ground of nightform_low_beam_take.mov is not flattened to Asphalt Black.
